name: Shoulder rotation
pattern: Rotation of the upper arm: with the elbow bent about 90° and the upper arm still, the forearm swings out (external rotation) or in (internal rotation) like a door on a hinge.
setup: Stand side-on to a band or cable set at elbow height.
Elbow bent 90°, upper arm by your side; a small rolled towel between elbow and ribs helps.
Stand tall, shoulder blade gently back and down.

steps.text: Start with the hand in front of your belly.
Turn the forearm out, away from your body, keeping the elbow at your side.
Stop when the forearm points forward-out at about 45-60°, or before your shoulder blade or trunk moves.
Let the hand come back in slowly.

cues.cue: Keep the elbow touching your side or the towel.
cues.why: If the elbow drifts, the deltoid joins in and the rotator cuff does less.

cues.cue: For the most cuff work, lie on your side with the top arm doing the rotation.
cues.why: Side-lying external rotation gave the highest infraspinatus (62% MVIC) and teres minor (67%) activity.

cues.cue: Shoulder blade back and down, not pinched hard; no shrug.
cues.why: Side-lying external rotation is one of the exercises with the best trapezius balance (low upper trap).

cues.cue: Rotate the arm, not your body.
cues.why: Turning the trunk fakes range and takes load off the cuff.
The cuff's main job is to steady and centre the ball of the shoulder; it does not need heavy loads to work.

breathing: Breathe normally; out as you rotate out.

tempo.note: Rotate out in about 2 seconds, hold, return in 3.

mistakes.name: Elbow lifts away
mistakes.looks: The elbow swings out from the side as the hand rotates.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze a towel between your elbow and ribs.
mistakes.why: Abducting the arm brings in the deltoid and supraspinatus instead of the external rotators.

mistakes.name: Trunk turns
mistakes.looks: The chest rotates away to move the band further.
mistakes.fix: Face forward; stop the rotation where your body would start to turn.
mistakes.why: The range comes from the spine, not the shoulder.

mistakes.name: Shoulder hikes or rolls forward
mistakes.looks: The shoulder rises or rolls forward as the arm turns.
mistakes.fix: Lighter band; shoulder blade gently back and down first.
mistakes.why: Upper-trapezius overuse and a tipped shoulder blade reduce the space for the cuff.

safety: After shoulder surgery or dislocation, follow your clinician's range limits; 90/90 rotation stresses the front of the shoulder.
Stop if you feel sharp pain or catching; a mild muscle burn is normal.
Rotation tests and mobility drills are for checking range, not for loading.

variants.change: Internal rotation: band from the outside, hand moves in toward the belly; works subscapularis and chest.
Isometric: press into a wall or towel without moving; good early in rehab.
Arm 30-45° out to the side and slightly forward (scapular plane): a comfortable middle position.
Rotation then press: rotate out at 90/90, then press the hand overhead.
A stick or the other hand moves the arm: mobility or a range test, not a strength set.

subtypes.name: Side-lying external rotation
subtypes.match: side lying|lying.*external|bench supported|lying shoulder|on a bench
subtypes.change: Lie on your side, top elbow bent 90° and resting on the ribs, towel under it; lift the weight by rotating the forearm up. The whole body is rolled 90° onto its side.

subtypes.name: 90/90 rotation
subtypes.change: Upper arm out to the side at shoulder height, elbow bent 90°; the forearm rotates from pointing forward up to vertical (and down for internal rotation).

subtypes.name: Internal rotation
subtypes.change: Band or cable from the outside; the hand moves from out to the side in toward the belly, elbow by the side.

easier: isometric external rotation against a wall

motion.basis: Exercise positions (0° with towel, side-lying, 90° abduction, scapular plane) from reinold2004; scapular balance from cools2007. Rotation end ranges are typical active ranges set by us (estimate); scapular retraction during external rotation is small and estimated; upward rotation at 90° abduction (about 20-25°) from ludewig2009 rhythm.
